subject: Operational egress catalog and per-tenant IP strategy for private connectors
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: AcmeCorp SRE <sre@acmecorp.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Operational egress catalog and per-tenant IP strategy for private connectors

Hi team — following up from last week's onboarding call with a concise set of asks so we can finalize the private-connectors runbook for your on‑prem deployment. Attached is an initial "egress catalog" (egress-catalog-draft.pdf) and a per‑tenant mapping workbook (tenant-egress-map.xlsx).

Goal: pick an operational model we can include in the contract appendix and the network appendix. Two leaning options below — please flag constraints (procurement, existing NAT IP limits, SOC controls) that would block either approach.

High level options
- Option A: Per-tenant static egress IPs (customer-owned NAT pool or assigned Redwood ephemeral IPs pinned per-tenant). Pros: straightforward ip-allowlisting in your firewall, simple billing attribution. Cons: IP lease management and rotation policy needed.
- Option B: Shared NAT + authenticated header assertion (shared IPs but requests carry an mTLS origin assertion/segment header to identify tenant). Pros: fewer public IPs to manage. Cons: requires egress header handling and firewall/proxy awareness on your side.

Immediate asks (can you reply in-line):
1) Provide the final list of external FQDNs/ports that must be reachable from the private connector (we've tried to pre-populate in tenant-egress-map.xlsx).
2) Confirm whether procurement requires ownership of the egress IPs (i.e., they will only sign if IPs are customer-controlled).
3) Any constraints on accepting asserted headers or mTLS client certs from our egress (Option B)?

Proposed next steps:
- We take your answers and produce a short addendum with: firewall rules (CIDR/port list), rotation policy for IPs, and the operational playbook for failover.
- Tentative followup workshop: Wed Dec 2 @ 11:00 PT to review items and lock the appendix.

Attachments: egress-catalog-draft.pdf (diagram + rationale), tenant-egress-map.xlsx (per-tenant rows).

Thanks — Marissa
-- 
Marissa Cole

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational egress catalog and per-tenant IP strategy for private connectors

Marissa — looping in some technical detail from the runtime/serving side. Happy to present these in the Dec 2 workshop.

Quick reactions:
- For predictable latency and simple firewalling, Option A (per-tenant static IPs) is the least surprising. We can ship either: (a) dedicated static IPs per-tenant from our managed pool, rotated on a scheduled cadence, or (b) support a customer-owned NAT gateway that peers to our private runtime.
- For Option B we can support a signed JWT in an X-Redwood-Tenant header + mTLS client cert on the egress tunnel. That requires your edge proxy to accept the header and map to internal tenant IDs; also preserves fewer public IPs.

FW rule snippets (attached fw-snippets.txt) include two canonical examples:
- Example A (per-tenant CIDR): allow tcp 443 to 34.198.55.12 (redwood-egress-tenant-001) from your outbound ACLs; include 30s connection idle timeout recommendations.
- Example B (shared NAT): allow tcp 443 to 34.198.0.0/18 and accept X-Redwood-Tenant header or mutual TLS with CN=redwood-egress.

Operational notes:
- Rotation: if we manage IPs we recommend a 90-day rotation window with a 7-day overlap window to avoid broken allowlists.
- Telemetry: we'll add per-tenant tags to logs (request-level) and provide a daily per-tenant egress summary so you can reconcile traffic.

I'll attach a one‑pager to the workshop.

-David
--
David Kim
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai
From: AcmeCorp SRE <sre@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmecorp.com, procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational egress catalog and per-tenant IP strategy for private connectors

Thanks Marissa & David — useful framing. A few items from AcmeCorp side: see inline below.

Inline answers:
1) FQDN/ports: attached is our minimal outbound whitelist we've historically required for third-party connectors. Essentials: *.redwood.ai (443), auth.redwood.ai (443), telemetry.redwood.ai (443), and azure-signing-endpoints used for key exchange. We'll upload a canonical CSV by EOD.
2) Procurement: our standard is to require customer-owned IPs for production SaaS access unless the vendor provides a security attestation and a formal IP-rotation SLA. That said, if Redwood can provide a signed attestation and is willing to include an IP-rotation appendix in the SOW, we can accept vendor-owned IPs for a 6‑month pilot.
3) Header assertion: security is open to header-based tenant assertion only if it is combined with mTLS and short-lived certs. Standalone header tracking is not sufficient for us.

Question: will Redwood's logs include source IP-to-tenant mapping? We need that for audit and incident response.

We can make Wed Dec 2 @ 11:00 PT but prefer a technical-only pre-meeting with your network lead 30 minutes before the full workshop.

— Alex (Acme SRE)
AcmeCorp SRE
sre@acmecorp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: AcmeCorp SRE <sre@acmecorp.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational egress catalog and per-tenant IP strategy for private connectors

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and for clarifying procurement's stance. Summary and proposed decision items so everyone is aligned before the workshop: 

1) Pilot approach: for the production pilot (first three tenants) we'll provision vendor-managed per-tenant static egress IPs with a signed attestation covering rotation windows and an SLA for IP change notifications. Procurement — can you confirm that a signed attestation + 30-day advance notice on rotation meets your requirement for the pilot?
2) Security gating: we'll implement Option A for the pilot and support mTLS + short-lived certs for control-plane/auth exchanges. Option B (shared NAT + assertions) remains our recommended long-term cost-optimization path but will require additional testing.
3) Logging/audit: yes — logs will include per-tenant source mapping and a daily CSV export. We'll surface this in the console and push the exports to the Drive folder linked below.

Action items before Wed workshop:
- Acme: upload canonical CSV of required FQDNs by EOD Mon Dec 6.
- Redwood (David): produce the firewall CIDR/port snippet file and an IP-rotation appendix draft by Dec 4.
- Redwood (Marissa): circulate a short procurement attestation template we can sign for the pilot.

If that looks good I'll lock the invite and set a 30-minute technical-only pre-call at 10:30 PT for David and your network folks.

Attachments referenced: fw-snippets.txt (David), egress-catalog-draft.pdf (Marissa).

Thanks — Marissa
